name: Sales Force
doc: Salesmen

name: Order Backlog
doc: Orders taken and not yet shipped

name: Capacity
doc: Units per month the plant can ship

name: Capacity on Order
doc: Capacity ordered and not yet working

name: Initial Capacity
doc: Production capacity at the start (equals orders at the start)

name: Target Delivery Delay
doc: Delivery delay the firm and its customers regard as normal

name: Minimum Delivery Time
doc: Shortest time from order to shipment when capacity is ample

name: Initial Sales Force
doc: Salesmen at the start

name: Orders per Salesman
doc: Orders one salesman brings in when the delivery delay is normal

name: Price
doc: Revenue per unit shipped

name: Salary Cost
doc: Cost of one salesman

name: Budget Fraction
doc: Share of revenue spent on the sales force (0.05 keeps the start in balance)

name: Hiring Time
doc: Time to bring the sales force to its budget

name: Delay Perception Time
doc: Time customers and the firm take to notice a change in delivery delay

name: Capacity Acquisition Time
doc: Time from ordering new capacity until it works

name: Delay Effect Switch
doc: 1 = a long delivery delay discourages orders; 0 = orders ignore the delay

name: Capacity Switch
doc: 1 = the firm orders capacity when delivery delay is long; 0 = capacity stays as it is

name: Sales Budget Switch
doc: 1 = the sales force follows revenue; 0 = the sales force stays at its starting size

name: Delay Effect on Orders
doc: Multiplier on orders as a function of the delay ratio

name: Capacity Order Fraction
doc: Fraction of capacity ordered per month, as a function of the delay ratio

name: Order Rate
equation: Sales Force * Orders per Salesman * Delay Effect Multiplier
doc: New orders

name: Shipments
equation: MIN(Capacity, Order Backlog / Minimum Delivery Time)
doc: Shipments: capacity, unless the backlog is nearly empty

name: Shipping
doc: Orders leaving the backlog as shipments

name: Delivery Delay
doc: Time an order waits: backlog over shipment rate

name: Perceived Delay
doc: Delivery delay as customers and the firm see it

name: Delay Effect Multiplier
equation: 1 + Delay Effect Switch * (Delay Effect on Orders(Delay Ratio) - 1)
doc: Effect of delivery delay on orders, after the switch

name: Target Sales Force
equation: IF THEN ELSE(Sales Budget Switch = 1, Budget Fraction * Revenue / Salary Cost, Initial Sales Force)
doc: Sales force the budget pays for

name: Sales Force Change
equation: (Target Sales Force - Sales Force) / Hiring Time
doc: Net hiring (negative = leaving)

name: Capacity Orders
equation: Capacity Switch * Capacity * Capacity Order Fraction(Delay Ratio)
doc: New capacity ordered

name: Capacity Completions
equation: Capacity on Order / Capacity Acquisition Time
doc: New capacity coming into use

name: Order to Capacity Ratio
doc: Above 1 the backlog is growing

problem: Does a growing firm stall because it cannot deliver fast enough, and does adding capacity in response to long delivery delays restore growth or only add swings?
out_of_scope: price changes, competitors, product quality, finance beyond a sales budget

title: Keep delivery near normal
test: Delivery delay stays within 1.5 times the target of 3 months for the 120 months.

title: Keep growing
test: Capacity at month 120 is at least double the starting 100 units per month.
